headline: US stocks closed higher as AI and semiconductor rally overshadowed easing US–Iran tensions and softer oil prices
raw_text:
- Major US indices ended higher, with the S&P 500 (SPY), Nasdaq, Dow (DIA) and Russell 2000 (IWM) all advancing as growth and tech leadership reasserted itself
- The S&P 500 (SPY) Information Technology sector outperformed, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) logged strong gains on renewed chip and AI enthusiasm
- Micron Technology (MU) rose after announcing a multibillion‑dollar US manufacturing investment tied to expanding AI-related demand
- Marvell Technology (MRVL), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Sandisk (SNDK) and ARM Holdings (ARM) each moved higher as investors rotated back into high‑beta semiconductor names
- Within the Magnificent Seven, Meta Platforms (META) rallied, while software lagged the broader tech sector, with Salesforce (CRM) and IBM (IBM) among notable decliners
- PepsiCo (PEP) declined after Q2 results showed EPS toward the low end of guidance despite a revenue beat
- Oil prices pulled back as markets downplayed renewed US–Iran tensions and near‑term supply risks in the Middle East
- In extended trading, Levi Strauss (LEVI) fell sharply despite reporting an earnings beat and raising guidance
- Traders are watching Delta Air Lines (DAL)’ earnings before Friday’s open along with a broader slate of corporate results
- Market participants are also focused on upcoming Fed-related commentary and ongoing Middle East and oil-market developments into the end of the week
